questions.prompt: G2 BRIEF — pulse (TypeScript monorepo: Fastify ingest, Redis Streams, vitest). Verified finding on the S13 PII fix: scrubProps only looks at the top-level keys of an event's props, so `props.user.email` or `props.contacts[0].phone` reaches the stream readable, and the HASH rule is a plain unsalted sha256, so the stored value of a known address is reproducible by anyone who can run sha256. You will delegate the fix to a coding agent. Write the brief: goal, allowed files, boundaries, test command, stop condition. Commit to your brief first, then tick the checkpoints you covered and add up the weights.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Goal: every DENY and HASH rule applies at any depth of props, inside nested objects and arrays, before the event is added to the stream, and HASH values come from a keyed hash under a server-held secret, so one input still maps to one stored value inside Pulse.

[w3] Guarded form: the walk is bounded (a fixed maximum depth, and a subtree beyond it is dropped, failing closed, never passed through), because props is an unbounded record of unknown values; the secret comes from validated env and production refuses to start without it instead of falling back to an unkeyed hash.

[w2] Scope includes keeping scrubProps pure and hash-injectable, with ingest receiving the keyed hasher through IngestServerOptions the way the rate limiter and quota check are injected, so tests control the key.

[w2] Allowed files: packages/shared/src/pii.ts and its test, apps/ingest/src/server.ts (the hasher at the scrub call), apps/ingest/src/env.ts (the secret), apps/ingest/src/index.ts (wiring) and apps/ingest/src/pii.test.ts.

[w3] Boundaries: backpressure, quota and rate-limit checks and their 429s stay exactly as they are; the rule names in DEFAULT_SCRUB_RULES do not change (no substring or pattern matching); no re-hashing or backfill of events already stored; the key-in-URL log redaction is not touched.

[w2] Test command: `pnpm --filter @pulse/shared test` and `pnpm --filter @pulse/ingest test` (each is vitest run); the ingest tests build the server on InMemoryKeyStore and InMemoryEventStream, so neither Redis nor Postgres is needed.

[w2] Stop condition: a new ingest test posts nested and array-held email and password values and asserts on what lands in the stream, red on the original and green on the fix, plus a test that one email hashes identically under one key and differently under another; the audit's quota and timestamp findings are reported, not fixed.

questions.prompt: G2 PRE-MORTEM — same delegation. What will an agent most likely get wrong here, and which line of your brief prevents it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] It recurses without a bound, so a deeply nested hostile payload overflows the stack and the error handler answers 500 after part of the batch is already queued, an availability bug in place of a privacy bug; the bounded, fail-closed walk prevents it.

[w3] It reads the secret with a default (an empty string or a constant) so a misconfigured deploy silently ships an unkeyed or publicly known hash; the 'validated env, refuse to start in production' line prevents it.
[w2] It scrubs in the consumer or at query time, so raw values still sit in the Redis stream; the goal says before the stream add, which is the whole point of the S13 remediation.

[w2] It 'improves' the rules in the same diff (matching any key containing 'email', lowercasing addresses before hashing), which changes which properties survive and which hashes join; the boundary freezes the rule names.
[w1] It keeps plain sha256 and points at the API-key ADR as precedent; that argument rests on 140-bit key entropy, which an email address does not have.

questions.prompt: G2 HANDBACK REVIEW — the agent hands back a diff and a green run. What do you check before accepting it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] The nested-scrub test goes through the ingest server, not just a unit call of scrubProps, and is shown red on the original server and green on the fix.
[w3] One implementation: ingest still calls scrubProps once per event before the stream add, with no second ad-hoc scrub inlined in server.ts.
[w2] The original scrub tests still pass unchanged, including case-insensitive matching and a null value on a hash key staying null.
[w2] The pasted output names both packages' vitest runs; the root `test` script goes through turbo, so a replayed cache hit is not evidence that the new tests ran.

[w1] The handback lists, without fixing, the audit findings the brief put out of scope, any sensitive key the exact rule names still miss, and the fact that hashes stored before the switch will not join new ones.
